about: Ad formats the guide can offer an owner, across static, carousel and video. Each format names the skill that makes it. The guide asks the owner for 'like your winners', 'a mix' or 'new formats', then picks formats with the rules in how_to_pick.
how_to_pick: Insight first, format second. Name the hypothesis (the objection, the education gap, the segment, the moment), then pick formats whose insight_fit includes it. A format that fits no stated insight does not go in the set.
Vary the format, not just the words. A set of 10 or more ads uses at least 3 different formats and at least 2 media where the owner can make them; near-copies of one template teach nothing.

Keep the proven winner's format as the control. 'Like your winners' means the winner's format with new angles plus one adjacent format; 'a mix' means one control in the winner's format and the rest in new formats; 'new formats' still keeps one control so the read is fair.

A format is allowed only when its needs are met. No real reviews means no review card or wall; no founder means no founder note; no real chat means the chat format is labelled as a dramatisation or swapped. Never fake a review, a message, a press mention or a countdown.

Native looks, brand truths. Notes, chat, text-thread and meme formats borrow the look of the feed, never a real person's words or a platform's own interface marks, and every claim inside them comes from the store's proof file.
Fit effort to the job. Same-day work uses low-effort formats; high-effort video goes in only when the owner has the people, footage or budget it needs.

formats.name: Product hero
formats.what: The real product big and sharp with one benefit line and a call to action.
formats.works_when: The buyer already knows the product or the category; retargeting and product-aware audiences.
formats.needs: A clean, accurate product photo; one approved benefit.
formats.risk: Looks like every other brand's ad; weak with cold audiences.

formats.name: Problem scene
formats.what: The moment the problem bites, with the product as a small inset or reveal.
formats.works_when: Problem-aware cold buyers who feel the pain but have not found a fix.
formats.needs: A problem buyers name in reviews or support tickets, in their own words.
formats.risk: Can feel negative or shaming if the scene mocks the buyer.

formats.name: Callout diagram
formats.what: Product in the centre with three or four labelled features pointing to it.
formats.works_when: Solution-aware buyers comparing details; products whose build quality is the reason to buy.
formats.needs: A spec sheet or product facts file that proves every label.
formats.risk: Feature lists without a reason to care read as a spec sheet.
formats.example_hook_shape: Every detail of [product], and why it is there.

formats.name: Comparison table
formats.what: A three to five row table: this product or option versus the usual way, a past version or a category standard.
formats.works_when: Buyers stuck between two options (for example two material grades or two price points) who need the trade-off made plain.
formats.needs: Measured, dated facts for both sides; a legally safe comparison target.
formats.risk: Naming a rival without proof breaks ad law in India and the US; keep it like for like.
formats.example_hook_shape: [Option A] vs [Option B]: which one is right for you?

formats.name: Review card
formats.what: One real review with the reviewer's name, rating, date and source.
formats.works_when: Warm buyers and cold skeptics who want to hear from someone like them.
formats.needs: A verified review export with permission to reuse; trim only, never reword.
formats.risk: Fake, staff or reworded reviews are banned; incentivised reviews must be labelled.
formats.example_hook_shape: "[Exact customer words about the result]" - [first name], verified buyer

formats.name: Review wall
formats.what: Three to six real reviews or customer photos on one image, each answering a different doubt.
formats.works_when: Warm buyers who need volume of proof; products with many photo reviews.
formats.needs: Several verified reviews with photos and reuse permission.
formats.risk: Crowded layouts become unreadable on a phone.
formats.example_hook_shape: [Number] people tried it. Here is what they said.

formats.name: Native post
formats.what: Looks like an ordinary feed post: plain background, message first, product second.
formats.works_when: Cold audiences that scroll past anything that looks like an ad.
formats.needs: One true, specific claim worth reading on its own.
formats.risk: If the message is generic, the native look buys nothing.

formats.name: Notes-app list
formats.what: A phone notes-style checklist (packing list, shopping list, things I wish I knew) with the product as one item.
formats.works_when: Planners and list-makers: gift buyers, wedding or trip prep, first-time buyers of a category.
formats.needs: A real buying routine or checklist buyers follow; the store's own type and colours, no platform interface marks.
formats.risk: Copying a platform's exact interface or using it as fake personal notes can mislead.

formats.name: Chat or DM screenshot
formats.what: A real customer message or pre-sale chat, shown as a screenshot with names hidden as the customer wishes.
formats.works_when: Trust gaps on a new brand, high-ticket items, or stores that sell by chat; shows real service.
formats.needs: The real message with the customer's written permission; date and source kept.
formats.risk: A made-up chat presented as real is a fake testimonial; label any dramatisation.
formats.example_hook_shape: "Will it arrive before [date]?" Here is what we told her.

formats.name: Text-message thread
formats.what: A short staged message thread between two people (friends, partners, a parent and child) where the product solves the problem.
formats.works_when: Gift buyers and shared decisions; humour or relatable moments for cold audiences.
formats.needs: A real buying situation from reviews or chats; a visible 'dramatisation' label if not real.
formats.risk: Reads as a testimonial if unlabelled; jokes can miss the brand voice.
formats.example_hook_shape: "What do I get [person] this year?" "Get the [product]."

formats.name: Founder note
formats.what: A real founder photo or handwritten-style note with one quote about why the product exists.
formats.works_when: Cold and warm buyers on a young brand where the maker is the difference.
formats.needs: A real founder, a real story and a real photo; never an AI-made founder.
formats.risk: Story claims need proof; a vague mission line wastes the format.

formats.name: Objection answer
formats.what: One objection in the buyer's words, one plain answer, one piece of proof.
formats.works_when: Bottom-of-funnel buyers who added to cart or asked the same question in chat.
formats.needs: Survey, chat or support data showing the objection, and proof that answers it.
formats.risk: Repeating a doubt the buyer never had can plant it.
formats.example_hook_shape: "Is it worth [price]?" Here is the honest answer.

formats.name: Offer card
formats.what: Price, offer, guarantee and end date on one clean card.
formats.works_when: Most-aware buyers waiting for a reason to buy now.
formats.needs: A live offer that matches the site word for word, break-even checked.
formats.risk: Trains buyers to wait for discounts; fake former prices are illegal.

formats.name: Bundle math
formats.what: Units, price per unit and the saving, laid out as simple sums.
formats.works_when: Repeat or most-aware buyers; consumables and sets.
formats.needs: A live bundle priced from real costs, break-even checked.
formats.risk: Wrong sums or a bundle that loses money on every order.

formats.name: How-it-works steps
formats.what: Three numbered steps showing how to use the product or how it works.
formats.works_when: Problem and solution-aware buyers unsure the product will be easy or will work for them.
formats.needs: Real instructions or a mechanism source.
formats.risk: Steps that make the product look like work.

formats.name: Before and after
formats.what: A split image of the same thing before and after the product, with honest labels.
formats.works_when: Products that make a visible, measurable difference.
formats.needs: Real, unretouched before and after photos under the same light; typical-results note.
formats.risk: Ad platforms reject health and body before-and-afters; retouching misleads.

formats.name: Myth vs fact
formats.what: A common belief about the category on the left, the true answer on the right.
formats.works_when: A category full of half-truths that stop people buying, or that make them buy the wrong thing.
formats.needs: A source for every fact; the myth must be something buyers really say.
formats.risk: Calling a rival's claim a myth without proof is disparagement.

formats.name: Category explainer
formats.what: A labelled teaching graphic: what a stamp, grade, ingredient or standard means and how to check it.
formats.works_when: Buyers who do not know how to judge quality in the category (for example what a purity mark means).
formats.needs: An official or primary source for the standard explained.
formats.risk: Teaching without a link back to the product earns attention but no sales.
formats.example_hook_shape: What does [mark or term] actually mean? Here is how to check.

formats.name: Price breakdown
formats.what: Where your money goes: the price split into materials, making, shipping and margin, or cost per use.
formats.works_when: Buyers who think the price is too high, or a brand whose pricing is its difference.
formats.needs: Real cost numbers the owner is willing to show; honest chart rules.
formats.risk: Showing costs that are wrong or invite a price fight.

formats.name: Press or award proof
formats.what: A real press quote, award or certification shown with its source and year.
formats.works_when: New-to-brand buyers who need outside proof before trusting a small store.
formats.needs: A real, dated press link or award certificate, and the right to quote it.
formats.risk: Implying an endorsement that was a paid placement, or an expired award.

formats.name: Countdown to a real event
formats.what: Days left to a real deadline: a festival, a delivery cutoff, or a sale with a real end date.
formats.works_when: Most-aware buyers before a dated moment, especially gift buyers near the last day to order.
formats.needs: A real date that matches the site and courier cutoffs; no fake timers.
formats.risk: Fake urgency is a banned dark pattern in India and a deceptive practice in the US.
formats.example_hook_shape: [n] days left to order for [festival] delivery.

formats.name: Seasonal moment
formats.what: The product placed in the rituals of one specific local moment, not a generic 'festive season'.
formats.works_when: A named moment that the buyer's region or community actually keeps (see moments.json).
formats.needs: The moment's real customs and dates from moments.json; stock and delivery for that window.
formats.risk: Getting a custom or date wrong insults the buyer you meant to honour.

formats.name: Meme format
formats.what: A familiar joke structure (two-panel, expectation vs reality) rebuilt with original art about the buyer's problem.
formats.works_when: Young, online audiences; low-cost tests for cold reach. Use with care.
formats.needs: Original images, not copyrighted meme photos; a joke that fits the brand voice.
formats.risk: Copyrighted images, dated jokes and off-brand tone; skip for premium or devotional moments.

formats.name: Long story ad
formats.what: One strong image with 200 to 500 words of true story in the primary text.
formats.works_when: Cold buyers who need more reasons; considered or high-ticket purchases.
formats.needs: A true story from the founder, a consenting customer or how the product is made.
formats.risk: Story that never earns the product; claims that need proof.
formats.example_hook_shape: [Unexpected first line of a true story]...

formats.name: Problem-proof-offer carousel
formats.what: Three to seven cards that move from the problem to proof to product to offer, one step per swipe.
formats.works_when: Products that need more than one image to explain; a single static is not converting.
formats.needs: Product photos, proof for each card, a live offer if one is shown.
formats.risk: A weak first card means nobody swipes.
formats.example_hook_shape: Card 1: [problem in buyer's words]. Swipe for the fix.

formats.name: Listicle carousel
formats.what: Numbered reasons, one per card: '5 reasons buyers switch'.
formats.works_when: Solution-aware buyers comparing options; products with several distinct benefits.
formats.needs: A proof line for every reason.
formats.risk: Padding the list with weak reasons.

formats.name: Lookbook carousel
formats.what: One product or collection styled several ways, one look per card.
formats.works_when: Apparel, jewellery and home buyers who need to picture it in their life.
formats.needs: An accurate campaign or lifestyle photo set for each look.
formats.risk: Pretty but no reason to buy now; product colour drift between photos.

formats.name: Gift guide
formats.what: Gifts sorted by recipient or budget, one card each, written for the giver.
formats.works_when: Gift buyers before a dated moment who do not know what to choose.
formats.needs: Gift-ready stock, real delivery cutoffs, gift wrap or message options that exist.
formats.risk: Promising delivery dates the courier cannot meet.

formats.name: "Which one are you" quiz
formats.what: A playful self-sorting carousel: pick your type, see your match.
formats.works_when: Ranges with several variants where buyers freeze on choice.
formats.needs: A real mapping from need or style to variant; a matching finder on the site helps.
formats.risk: Types that flatter but do not help choose.
formats.example_hook_shape: Which [product] are you? Swipe to find out.

formats.name: Size and fit guide
formats.what: How to measure and which size to pick, shown card by card with a model's size worn.
formats.works_when: Apparel, footwear, rings and fitted goods where fit doubt blocks the sale or drives returns.
formats.needs: Real measurements, return reasons and fit notes.
formats.risk: Wrong measurements raise returns instead of cutting them.
formats.example_hook_shape: Not sure of your size? Here is how to check in 30 seconds.

formats.name: Catalog or dynamic product ad
formats.what: Feed-driven ads that show each viewer products they browsed, with a branded frame and true price.
formats.works_when: Large catalogues; product-aware retargeting.
formats.needs: A clean product feed whose prices match the site; overlay rules per product set.
formats.risk: Stale sale prices, borrowed ratings and badges that are false for some items.

formats.name: Unboxing
formats.what: The real parcel, packaging, contents and first use, exactly as a buyer gets them.
formats.works_when: Gift-able products with good packaging; buyers worried about what arrives.
formats.needs: A real order through the store, filmed as delivered.
formats.risk: Plain packaging or slow delivery shown on camera hurts; staged parcels mislead.

formats.name: Customer testimonial video
formats.what: A real customer on their phone saying what changed, cut to 20 to 40 seconds.
formats.works_when: Trust gaps and objections that a peer answers better than the brand.
formats.needs: Real customers with written consent, a rights log, non-leading questions.
formats.risk: Editing that changes what the customer meant; missing disclosure of any thank-you.
formats.example_hook_shape: "I almost did not buy it because [objection]."

formats.name: Street interview
formats.what: Quick questions to real people in public, with a product test or reaction on camera.
formats.works_when: Cold reach for a product whose result shows in seconds; testing a myth with real people.
formats.needs: Real passers-by with signed releases on the spot; an honest test.
formats.risk: Planted actors passed off as strangers mislead; consent is easy to skip.
formats.example_hook_shape: We asked strangers to [test]. Most got it wrong.

formats.name: Creator talking head
formats.what: A creator tells one buyer's story to camera, with the demo answering the main objection.
formats.works_when: Cold audiences that trust people over brands; products with a story to tell.
formats.needs: A creator who has really used the product; usage rights and disclosure.
formats.risk: Read-sounding scripts and claims the creator cannot back.
formats.example_hook_shape: I was [buyer moment] when I found this.

formats.name: Founder to camera
formats.what: The founder tells the true origin story or answers a doubt directly.
formats.works_when: A real origin story; small brands where the founder is the trust.
formats.needs: A founder willing to record, or their voice or evidence; a fact sheet for every claim.
formats.risk: Story claims without proof; stiff delivery.
formats.example_hook_shape: I am the founder, and here is what we refused to do.

formats.name: Day in the life
formats.what: A real day of the buyer type, with the product in its true place in the routine.
formats.works_when: Lifestyle products and segments that want to see someone like them using it.
formats.needs: A creator or customer who matches the segment; honest use.
formats.risk: The product gets lost in the vlog.
formats.example_hook_shape: A day as a [buyer type], and the one thing I always carry.

formats.name: Reply to a comment
formats.what: A video that answers a real comment or question shown on screen.
formats.works_when: A real question many buyers ask; good for objections and education.
formats.needs: A real comment or question, used with care for the commenter's privacy.
formats.risk: Invented comments look fake fast.

formats.name: Green-screen reaction
formats.what: A presenter reacts in front of a screenshot, chart, review or myth.
formats.works_when: Education and myth-busting; reacting to a category habit buyers dislike.
formats.needs: A real source image the brand may show; a presenter.
formats.risk: Showing a rival's content can break ad law or copyright.
formats.example_hook_shape: This is what [category] does not want you to know about [topic].

formats.name: "3 reasons" list video
formats.what: A fast spoken list: three reasons, one per beat, with on-screen numbers.
formats.works_when: Solution-aware buyers; products with several real benefits.
formats.needs: Proof for each reason.
formats.risk: Reason three is filler.

formats.name: 15-second demo
formats.what: The main benefit proven on screen in one take, with a 6-second cut.
formats.works_when: Products whose value a muted viewer can see happen.
formats.needs: The real product doing the job, filmed without speed-ups or tricks.
formats.risk: Sped-up or staged demos mislead and get rejected.

formats.name: Split-screen
formats.what: Two halves side by side: the old way and the product, or two options doing the same task.
formats.works_when: A visible difference against the usual way.
formats.needs: A fair, like-for-like test filmed for real.
formats.risk: An unfair setup is a misleading comparison.

formats.name: ASMR or close-up
formats.what: Wordless, satisfying close-ups of the product's texture, sound or motion.
formats.works_when: Tactile products; openers that stop the scroll without a presenter.
formats.needs: The real product, good light, its own sounds recorded.
formats.risk: Draws watchers, not buyers, unless the moment ties to a benefit.
formats.example_hook_shape: (no words) [pour, fold or texture moment] then [benefit text].

formats.name: Animated explainer
formats.what: A 30 to 40 second animation of why a problem happens, then the product as the fix.
formats.works_when: Problems with a hidden cause; education gaps a static cannot show.
formats.needs: A primary source for the mechanism and proof that this product does it.
formats.risk: A mechanism the product does not really use is a false claim.

formats.name: Podcast clip
formats.what: A clip that looks like two people talking on a podcast, where the product comes up naturally.
formats.works_when: Considered purchases; audiences that listen to long-form talk.
formats.needs: Two distinct hosts, a script from the facts file, and an on-screen 'staged and paid' label.
formats.risk: Passing a staged clip off as a real show misleads.
formats.example_hook_shape: "Wait, you have been [doing it wrong] this whole time?"

formats.name: Stylised animation
formats.what: A clay, comic-page or talking-product style scene that ends on the real product.
formats.works_when: Feeds tired of live action; brands with a playful voice. Test one scene first.
formats.needs: A locked style card and an exact real product at the reveal.
formats.risk: Costly to make; style can bury the product.

formats.name: Photo to motion
formats.what: Three to six second clips made from existing product photos with camera moves.
formats.works_when: Stores with good photos but no video; quick openers and b-roll.
formats.needs: High-quality product photos; an accuracy check on every frame.
formats.risk: Generated motion that warps the product.
